headline_marked: [[Hacked Ledger wallets with secret eSIM chips]] siphoned $93M+ from users via compromised resellers
headline: Hacked Ledger wallets with secret eSIM chips siphoned $93M+ from users via compromised resellers
summary: Hardware crypto wallets bought from third-party resellers in Asia and Europe were found to contain hidden chips that steal recovery phrases.
details: An ongoing investigation has revealed that Ledger hardware wallets purchased from third-party resellers in Southeast Asia and Europe were compromised with secret eSIM and LTE modules. These hidden components were designed to exfiltrate users' recovery phrases, leading to over $93 million in siphoned funds.

The data theft occurs during the initial setup process. A flexible PCB hidden under the display assembly captures the pixels showing the private key as it's entered, then transmits this information via the embedded eSIM+LTE combination.

Initial reports traced compromised units to reseller Cryptobilis in Malaysia, which has since ceased hardware wallet sales. More recently, hacked wallets with identical modifications were discovered at MediaMarkt in Germany, suggesting a wider, potentially coordinated operation.

Ledger advises users who bought wallets from Cryptobilis within the last 90 days not to perform the initial setup. For those who have already set up a potentially compromised wallet, the company recommends moving all assets to a new wallet with a new seed phrase.

While Ledger-direct purchases appear unaffected, the discovery of manufactured-to-order hardware implants in the latest hacked wallets raises concerns. This suggests a potential production line dedicated to intercepting and modifying Ledger devices in bulk.

Users are encouraged to verify the physical integrity of their wallets against official Ledger component pictures. Additionally, always download software exclusively from the official Ledger website URL to avoid scam sites distributing booby-trapped software.

topic: ai impact on wikipedia usage decline
headline_marked: [[AI content pervades Wikipedia]], leading to outright ban of LLMs for writing
headline: AI content pervades Wikipedia, leading to outright ban of LLMs for writing
summary: A 2024 study found 5% of new English Wikipedia articles contained substantial AI content, leading to a full ban on LLMs for article writing by March 2026.
details: Wikipedians initially believed AI would automate housekeeping and free up humans for creative work, but this proved overly optimistic. The Wikimedia Foundation had been making preparations long before the "storm of AI" struck.

By 2018, Google was already training AI to write "Wikipedia-like articles." A 2024 Princeton study found that about 5 percent of nearly 3,000 newly created English Wikipedia articles in a single month (August 2024) contained substantial AI-generated content.

Early AI content often showed tell-tale signs like em dashes, curly quotation marks, and even residues from prompts. Wikipedians initially tried to shape and control AI output, weeding out generic fluff and fake sources.

However, by March 2026, AI content was found to violate Wikipedia's core principles so frequently that writing with large language models was banned outright. Their role was restricted to translation and minor proofreading.

A much-read essay titled "Death of Wikipedia" explained this defensive posture, predicting a ripple effect. As human contributors reduced their work due to AI's prevalence, there might be a temptation to replace them with even more AI, creating a downward spiral.

The essay warned that instead of AI performing "housekeeping," it might compose articles, leaving humans relegated to formatting and cleanup. This would trap editors in an endless curatorial project derived from machines, not human priorities.

The potential "whittling down" of talented writers is seen as the greatest threat, as it would lead to a "sprawling hellscape of weak, inaccurate and incomplete articles." A machine-written Wikipedia risks becoming artless and soulless.

With Google's AI Overviews becoming central to search, Wikipedia still plays a crucial role as a source, albeit one step removed. If Wikipedia itself becomes corrupted by AI, the means to prove when AI agents are wrong will be compromised, as they often give plausible but incorrect answers.
